local_validation.host_previews: none new: this version adds an optional model and a Settings row (checked by tests that read the Settings source, not by a render)
local_validation.beat_model: Beat This! small (MIT) converted by publish-beat-model.yml to a fixed [1, 500, 128] input with float16 weights, published as prerelease ketmix-beat-v1 (18,575,568 bytes, SHA-256 74cc5ee9...). It was compared with the original ONNX only on random input (mean relative difference about 0.5 percent on the matching outputs) and on a synthetic pulse (5 to 7 percent, only one clear peak, which was found). It was never fine-tuned, never run on a real song and never compared with Ketmix's own analysis, and it is not bundled in the APK. 30 s and 15 s windows were rejected: attention tensors grow with the square of the length (about 288 MB per tensor at 30 s). The pure-Kotlin log-mel front end matches a numpy re-implementation (max difference under 2e-3); its parameters come from the Beat This! source read on PyPI
local_validation.after_local_run: the full local run (mobile 1671, quest 1661, lite 1669 tests, lint without errors) had one failure, BeatModelTest.theRowHasItsTranslations reading a deleted pending file; the test now reads the bundled catalog, was rerun with BeatModelTest and BeatSettingsRowTest (18 tests) and passed in CI on the final commit
local_validation.sdk_30: Robolectric's Android 11 runtime could not be downloaded in the cloud container (Maven Central answered 429), so the Lite tests that declare sdk 30 ran on sdk 31 only; nothing ran on an Android 11 runtime

known_limitations: No Wear OS app in this version.
Seasonal themes use code-drawn decor until the owner's pictures are added.
Android Auto's queue screen shows only the current song.
Switching between Ketvoice and Ketvoice Lite is a manual install of the other APK.
Ketogether guests hear titles their own sources can play; local files and private titles are shown as unavailable.
Launcher icons keep a background: Android fills adaptive icon backgrounds in black.
The signing certificate is the existing public Android debug identity, not a private production key.
